title: Calculating donor retention rates on Mac: how to fix your nonprofit data reporting
metaTitle: Calculating donor retention rates: fix nonprofit data reporting on Mac
description: Stop struggling with manual data reconciliation. Learn how to calculate donor retention rates efficiently on your Mac without expensive software.
intro: Calculating donor retention rates is often the biggest hurdle for nonprofit fundraisers working on a Mac. You likely spend hours manually cleaning spreadsheets just to see if your donor base is growing or shrinking.
tldr: Stop manually reconciling donor lists across multiple spreadsheets.
Use standardized data collection to feed your reporting tools.
Leverage built-in Mac tools to speed up data entry.
Focus on donor retention rates as a primary metric for success.

blocks.text: The hidden cost of manual data reporting

When you are constantly switching between your CRM, email, and Excel, you lose focus. This is the admin tax. You are not just entering data. You are acting as the bridge between systems that do not talk to each other.
Why calculating donor retention rates feels impossible

The primary cause is data fragmentation. You might have one list of donors in Salesforce and another in a local Excel file. When you try to combine them, you find duplicate entries with different spellings. This is the matching problem.

items: Inconsistent data entry rules across team members.
Disconnected tools that require manual file exports.
Lack of a single source of truth for donor history.
Fear of breaking complex formulas in your master spreadsheet.

blocks.text: Fixing your data workflow on Mac

You do not need an expensive consultant to start fixing your reporting. Start by standardizing your intake forms. If you use Jotform or Google Forms, ensure the output format matches your master spreadsheet exactly.

items: Use data validation in Excel to force consistent donor categories.
Create a master donor file that uses unique IDs instead of just names.
Automate your exports so you are not manually downloading CSV files.
Use pivot tables to group donations by year automatically.

blocks.text: How Lazur helps with your fundraising data
Lazur lives in your Mac notch. It sees your screen and hears your questions. When you are stuck in Excel trying to remember a formula or find a specific setting, ask Lazur.

Many fundraisers try to report on too many metrics at once. Focus on retention first. If you cannot track who gave last year and who gave this year, you cannot calculate retention. Simplify your spreadsheet to show only the donor ID, the year of the gift, and the amount.

faq.question: How do I calculate donor retention rates in Excel?
faq.answer: Divide the number of donors who gave in both the current and previous year by the total number of donors from the previous year. Use a pivot table in Excel to group your data by donor ID and year first.

faq.question: Is it safe to use AI for donor data?
faq.answer: Always follow your organization's data privacy policies. Never upload sensitive PII (Personally Identifiable Information) to public AI tools. If you use Lazur, it does not store your screen data.

causes.title: Data fragmentation
causes.text: Donor information lives in too many places, including legacy CRMs, email chains, and local spreadsheets.

causes.title: Lack of integration
causes.text: Your tools do not talk to each other, forcing you to act as the manual integration layer.

causes.title: Inconsistent data entry
causes.text: Without standardized forms, donor names and records are entered differently, making them impossible to match.

fixes.title: Standardize your intake
fixes.text: Use strict validation rules on your forms to ensure data enters your system in a clean, consistent format.

fixes.title: Consolidate your records
fixes.text: Move toward a single record per donor that links to all their historical notes and gifts.

fixes.title: Automate data exports
fixes.text: Use tools like Zapier to move data from your forms directly into your reporting spreadsheet.
